result.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
result.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the full set of (state, policy-action) pairs along the policy's visited distribution. We instantiate the surrogate with three interpretable model families (decision trees, linear regression, and logistic regression) and compare their fidelity and task return. We evaluate ReShap on Atari and Box2D environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct a human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the resulting policies. Results show that ReShap preserves competitive task performance, that decision trees generally outperform linear and logistic regression, and that linear regression is weakest in most settings.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 ReShap，将基于 Shapley 值的可解释性扩展到高维图像观测与多动作的深度 RL 策略：从原始图像提取紧凑特征并做 SHAP 特征归因，再把策略蒸馏为决策树、线性或逻辑回归等可解释代理，在 Atari、Box2D 上比较保真度与任务回报，并辅以人类被试研究。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「压缩视觉特征—逐特征贡献归因—可解释代理核查」流程可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 内容贡献分配提供评价思路，但对象是 RL 动作策略而非多模态推理状态，迁移需较多核查。
